questions.subtopic: Head Noun Isolation with Complex Prepositional Chain
questions.question:
In the sentence below, identify the segment with a grammatical error:
"(A) The detailed expenditure report / (B) for the procurement of modern laptops / (C) have been forwarded to the finance department / (D) for statutory auditing."

options.text: for the procurement of modern laptops
have been forwarded to the finance department

questions.explanation: Segment (C) mein error hai. Sentence ka grammatical Head Noun 'The detailed expenditure report' (singular) hai. 'for the procurement of modern laptops' prepositional modifiers hain. Singular head noun ke sath singular auxiliary 'HAS been forwarded' aani chahiye, 'have been' proximity error hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Head Noun Isolation vs Intervening Prepositional Phrases
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L13 Certification

questions.question:
Choose the correct verb form to complete the sentence:
"The senior judicial magistrate, together with several local police inspectors, ___ arriving at the spot for spot inspection."
questions.explanation: 'Together with' ek parenthetical connective hai. Sentence ka grammatical subject strictly FIRST SUBJECT ('The senior judicial magistrate' [singular]) hai. Iske sath singular verb 'is arriving' aayegi.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-04: Parenthetical Connectives & The First-Subject Rule
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L13 Certification

questions.question:
Select the option that correctly completes the sentence:
"Neither the advocates nor the client ___ willing to accept the proposed settlement out of court."
questions.explanation: In 'Neither ... nor', Proximity Rule lagta hai. Verb apne physically nearest subject ke number se agree karti hai. Verb position ke sabse paas 'the client' (singular noun) hai, isliye singular past auxiliary 'was' aayegi.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-03: Correlative Conjunctions & The Proximity Rule
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L13 Certification

questions.question:
Identify the incorrect part of the sentence:
"(A) In the high-profile inquiry, / (B) neither of the two primary suspects / (C) were willing to disclose / (D) the source of the leaked government document."

options.text: neither of the two primary suspects
the source of the leaked government document.

questions.explanation: Segment (C) mein error hai. 'Neither of + plural noun' construction distributive singular hoti hai aur strictly SINGULAR VERB leti hai. Isliye 'were willing to disclose' ke bajaye 'was willing to disclose' aana chahiye.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-05: Distributive Singular Pronouns: Each, Every, Either of, Neither of
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L13 Certification

questions.question:
Fill in both blanks with the grammatically correct pair of verbs:
"A number of system assistants ___ deployed to monitor the digital servers, while the number of critical server alerts ___ steadily declining."
questions.explanation: 'A number of + plural noun' ka matlab 'many' hota hai ➔ PLURAL auxiliary 'have been'. 'The number of + plural noun' ka subject 'The number' (singular count) hota hai ➔ SINGULAR auxiliary 'is'. Sahi pair 'have been / is' hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-07: 'A Number of' (Plural) vs 'The Number of' (Singular)
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L13 Certification

questions.subtopic: Relative Clause Antecedent Concord: 'One of the... Who'
questions.question:
Spot the error in the sentence:
"(A) This is one of the most / (B) well-reasoned constitutional judgments / (C) that has ever been delivered / (D) by the full bench of this High Court."

options.text: This is one of the most
by the full bench of this High Court.

questions.explanation: Segment (C) mein error hai. Relative pronoun 'that' ka antecedent uske theek pehle aane wala plural noun 'constitutional judgments' hai. Plural antecedent hone ke karan relative clause ke andar plural verb 'HAVE ever been delivered' aani chahiye, 'has' incorrect hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-08: 'One of the' Relative Clause Concord vs 'The Only One'
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L13 Certification

questions.question: Choose the grammatically correct sentence from the following options:

options.text: Sunita is the only one of the judicial stenographers who have completed the transcription without error.
Sunita is the only one of the judicial stenographers who has completed the transcription without error.
Sunita is one of the only judicial stenographer who have completed the transcription without error.
Sunita are the only one of the judicial stenographers who has completed the transcription without error.

questions.explanation: Option B is correct. Jab 'THE ONLY ONE' clause aata hai, toh focus pure group se restrict hokar sirf Sunita (singular) par aa jata hai. Isliye relative pronoun 'who' ke baad singular verb 'has completed' aayegi.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-08: 'One of the' Relative Clause Concord vs 'The Only One'
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L13 Certification

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the appropriate auxiliary verb:
"The special investigation team ___ submitted its preliminary report in a sealed envelope to the division bench."
questions.explanation: Collective noun 'The special investigation team' ke baad singular neuter pronoun 'ITS preliminary report' diya gaya hai. Poori team ek single document submit kar rahi hai. Unified sense mein collective noun singular hota hai, isliye singular auxiliary 'has' aayegi.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: Collective Nouns: Unitary Sense vs Divided Members
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L13 Certification

questions.question:
Identify the incorrect part of the sentence:
"(A) Following the intense deliberations, / (B) the jury was completely divided / (C) in their opinions regarding / (D) the circumstantial evidence presented by the prosecution."

options.text: the circumstantial evidence presented by the prosecution.

questions.explanation: Segment (B) mein error hai. Sentence mein 'divided' aur 'their opinions' aane ki wajah se jury Noun of Multitude (plural) ban chuki hai. Isliye 'the jury was completely divided' ke bajaye 'the jury WERE completely divided' aana chahiye.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: Collective Nouns: Unitary Sense vs Divided Members
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L13 Certification

questions.subtopic: Quantities & Measurements: Time Duration as a Unit
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the grammatically correct verb:
"Three hours ___ the standard allotted duration for the written competitive examination."
questions.explanation: 'Three hours' ek single unbroken time period / duration (indicated by 'the standard allotted duration') hai. Jab time duration ek single block ke roop mein express ho, toh verb strictly SINGULAR ('is') aati hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09A: Quantities, Measurements, Time, Distance & Money as Single Units
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L13 Certification

questions.question:
In the sentence below, identify the segment with an agreement error:
"(A) According to the inspection report, / (B) there was several procedural anomalies / (C) observed during the maintenance of / (D) the official digital register."
questions.explanation: Segment (B) mein error hai. 'There' introductory placeholder hai; actual subject verb ke baad aane wala noun phrase 'several procedural anomalies' (plural) hai. Plural subject ke sath plural verb 'there WERE several procedural anomalies' aayegi.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10: Inverted Word Order & Dummy 'There' Concord
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L13 Certification

questions.question:
Spot the error in the sentence:
"(A) During the judicial recruitment drive, / (B) many a deserving candidate / (C) have been disqualified / (D) due to minor clerical discrepancies in their certificates."

options.text: due to minor clerical discrepancies in their certificates.

questions.explanation: Segment (C) mein error hai. 'Many a + Singular Noun' construction formal syntax mein strictly SINGULAR VERB leti hai. Isliye 'have been disqualified' ke bajaye 'HAS been disqualified' hona chahiye.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-11: 'Many a' & 'More than one' Idiomatic Concord
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L13 Certification

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the appropriate verb form:
"The Chief Justice and the Law Secretary ___ arrived together to inspect the new digital record room."
questions.explanation: Dono designations ke aage alag-alag definite article 'The' laga hai ('THE Chief Justice and THE Law Secretary'). Iska matlab do alag-alag vyakti hain (2 Persons = Plural Compound Subject). Plural subject ke sath plural auxiliary 'have arrived' aayegi.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-02: Compound Subjects with 'AND': Two Entities vs Single Notion
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L13 Certification

questions.subtopic: Variable Indefinite Pronouns: SANAM Rule with Plural Noun
questions.question:
Choose the correct option to fill in the blank:
"Most of the computer terminals installed in the public registry ___ upgraded with the latest antivirus definition files."
questions.explanation: SANAM variable pronoun 'Most' ke baad 'of the computer terminals' (plural countable noun) aaya hai. Jab SANAM pronoun plural countable noun ko refer kare, toh verb strictly PLURAL ('have been') hoti hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-06: Variable Quantity Indefinite Pronouns: The SANAM Complement Law
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L13 Certification

questions.subtopic: Plural Title of Book / Creative Work
questions.question:
Spot the error in the sentence:
"(A) The Arabian Nights, / (B) which contains numerous fascinating tales / (C) of Eastern folklore, / (D) are highly regarded in world literature."

options.text: are highly regarded in world literature.

questions.explanation: Segment (D) mein error hai. 'The Arabian Nights' ek single world-famous collection of tales ka title hai. Bhale hi iske title mein 'Nights' plural lagta hai, ye ek single literary work hai aur strictly SINGULAR VERB 'IS highly regarded' leta hai, 'are' incorrect hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Head Noun Isolation vs Intervening Prepositional Phrases
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L13 Certification
